A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolPRM study. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A and B, which were inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model training results and function-calling evaluations on BFCL and ToolAlpaca in Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds self-reflection comparisons, a masking ablation, constrained-decoding comparisons and API-Bank evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The intra-call decomposition, supervision labels, state transitions, training objective and ToolPRM-guided beam search remain unchanged. Appendix B clarifies that masking affects only part of the training data; it does not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds evaluation on cleaned API-Bank dialogues, covering both invocation of a known API (L1) and selection from candidate APIs (L2). The original training datasets and BFCL/ToolAlpaca benchmark coverage remain.

E2.justification: Appendix B adds BFCL comparisons against self-reflection variants of Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-32B, and against FANTASE with a RoBERTa reranker. FANTASE was cited but not evaluated in v1. The comparator sets in the original main tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments keep their training settings, metrics and beam-parameter sweeps. New appendix experiments introduce masking-disabled training controls, self-reflection conditions and FANTASE reranking trained on the shared dataset. API-Bank evaluation uses a cleaned collection of 314 dialogues and 753 API calls; these are new protocols, not documented changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a function-masking ablation and an analysis of self-reflection motivated by structural-error recovery. Conversely, Section 4.4 and Figure 4 remove the two BFCL budget-scaling analyses, retaining only the ToolAlpaca analyses. The original reward-granularity comparison remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional appendix results continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the retained ToolAlpaca curves are unchanged. New entries in Tables 4–7 include unmasked ToolPRM scoring 84.90 versus masked ToolPRM's 85.61 BFCL average, FANTASE scoring 84.27, and ToolPRM API-Bank average F1 scores of 94.35 (L1) and 78.11 (L2). Self-reflection results are added, while BFCL budget-scaling results are removed.

T1.justification: The formal trajectory description, state definitions, reward-training objective and scoring formula remain equivalent. The appendices add empirical arguments, without new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central scientific contributions: the first fine-grained intra-call supervision dataset, ToolPRM-guided inference scaling, and the 'explore more but retain less' principle. The shorter abstract and revised introduction preserve these claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds limitations concerning discretized supervision, implicit reasoning, global optimality and sensitivity to masking/state definitions. Appendix B newly interprets limited reflection gains as support for practical unrecoverability, masking as regularization, and constrained decoding plus reranking as insufficient to match fine-grained supervision.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies a generation-prompt template. Appendix B clarifies partial training-data masking and documents the FANTASE reranker and cleaned API-Bank collection. Main implementation details remain unchanged, while v1's statement that code and checkpoints are publicly accessible is removed. Masking proportions and the self-reflection procedure remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The literature coverage is substantially pruned and revised. Discussions and citations concerning Octopus, TinyAgent, NESTful, ComplexFuncBench and R-PRM disappear, while PARL-MT, latent verifiers, StepORLM, retrieval-augmented PRMs and newer surveys enter. The central positioning around previously underexplored intra-call supervision remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten and condensed. Numbered related-work subsections become shorter topical paragraphs, Section 4.4 is rewritten, and standalone Limitations, Acknowledgements and appendix sections are added. Author information and placeholder headers are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and page layout, substantially shrinks and relocates Figures 3–4, and redraws Figure 4 with two ToolAlpaca panels and revised legends/axes instead of four benchmark panels. It adds Tables 4–7 and Listing 1. The main tables retain their numerical content despite resizing and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The masking ablation, FANTASE comparison and API-Bank tests add useful validation absent from v1, while the prompt and limitations improve transparency. These benefits are tempered by removal of the BFCL scaling curves and incomplete documentation of the new reflection experiment. Its final-accuracy results also do not directly establish error unrecoverability, limiting the strength of the added support.
